web_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
book_title: Chapter 7: Why the Price Is What It Is — Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
question: At ₹1,914.40 per share (₹8,145–₹8,189 crore market cap), what exact cash-flow and margin trajectory is the market already pricing into AXISCADES' retained Defence and Aerospace platform?

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; implied expectations are what you underwrite. When a stock trades at forty times normalized operating profit during a corporate carve-out, you are no longer buying a turnaround—you are prepaying for flawless execution.
epigraph.author: Institutional Valuation Desk Maxim

web_blocks.title: Reconciling the P/E Mirage: 1,993x vs. 226.15x vs. 113x

web_blocks.html: On 13 November 2026, two market terminals show a jarring P/E gap for AXISCADES. Screener displays a trailing P/E of 1,993x on a ₹8,189 crore market cap (10.8x Book Value of ₹177 per share) [1]. TradingView prints a trailing P/E of 226.15x on a ₹8,144.95 crore market cap at ₹1,914.40 [23]. Both figures reflect different accounting filters during an Ind AS 105 carve-out. Neither is usable without normalization.

The gap stems from the multi-phase Akkodis divestment (effective transfer 1 October 2026), covering Heavy Engineering, Automotive, Energy, and Aerospace Services [9][10]. Under Ind AS 105, disposal-group results leave continuing operations. That puts TTM continuing sales at ₹831 crore and operating profit at ₹78 crore (9.4% OPM) [1]. Reported TTM Net Profit is ₹61 crore, but ₹69 crore came from non-operating Other Income [1]. Q2 FY27 alone booked +₹61 crore of restructuring adjustments [1][8]. Meanwhile, H1 FY27 absorbed ₹21.81 crore of deal fees, ₹11.56 crore of aged defence receivable provisions, and ₹12 crore of ESOP costs [8]. Screener strips out Other Income, leaving ~₹4.1 crore of adjusted profit (₹8,189 Cr / ₹4.1 Cr ≈ 1,993x) [1]. TradingView uses unadjusted diluted TTM EPS of ~₹8.47 (₹1,914.40 / ₹8.47 = 226.15x) [23]. Pre-carve-out FY26 consolidated EPS was ₹16.92 (₹72 crore PAT), or 113.1x earnings [1][23].

web_blocks.title: Sum-of-the-Parts (SOTP) Valuation: Retained Platform + Net Akkodis Cash

web_blocks.html: Because Ind AS 105 breaks trailing P/E, we value AXISCADES via a Sum-of-the-Parts (SOTP) bridge. Part (a) values the retained core: Defence Electronics (Mistral Solutions), Aerospace Manufacturing/MRO, ESAI, and Space [8]. Part (b) adds net cash from the ~₹2,256 crore Akkodis sale after taxes, deal costs, and debt payoff [8][10].

Retained continuing revenue reached ₹378.95 crore in H1 FY27 (+55% YoY) [8]. Q2 FY27 continuing revenue hit ₹195.6 crore (+30.3% YoY, +6.7% QoQ) [8]. With H2 Mistral delivery seasonality, FY27E retained sales track toward ₹840 crore (range ₹820–₹860 crore). Excluding carve-out and ESOP costs, a 20% EBITDA margin yields ₹168 crore of normalized FY27E EBITDA. Growing 30% in FY28E to ₹1,092 crore at a 21% margin produces ₹229 crore of FY28E EBITDA.

web_blocks.takeaway: Even on generous FY28E normalized earnings (₹229 Cr EBITDA at 28x) plus full net Akkodis cash (₹1,152 Cr), SOTP fair value is ₹1,771/share—7.5% below the ₹1,914.40 market price [1][8][10].

web_blocks.the_number: ₹1,770 per share (FY28E SOTP Base Fair Value; Implied Retained EV ₹7,037 Cr at CMP)
web_blocks.how_calculated: We deduct ₹1,152 crore of pro-forma net Akkodis cash (₹2,256 crore gross proceeds minus ₹406 crore estimated tax/closing drag and ₹698 crore Sep 2026 gross debt) from the ₹8,189 crore market cap to isolate an implied ₹7,037 crore Enterprise Value for the retained business, then compare that against FY27E/FY28E normalized EBITDA and a 10-year Reverse DCF.
web_blocks.the_inputs: CMP ₹1,914.40; diluted shares ~4.27 crore; H1 FY27 retained revenue ₹378.95 crore (+55% YoY); FY27E retained revenue ₹840 crore at 20% normalized EBITDA margin (₹168 crore); FY28E retained revenue ₹1,092 crore at 21% EBITDA margin (₹229 crore); WACC 12.0%, terminal growth 5.0%, 25% tax rate.
web_blocks.the_range: ₹1,207/share (conservative 25x FY27E EBITDA + ₹952 Cr net cash) to ₹2,450/share (bull 31x FY28E EBITDA of ₹300 Cr + ₹1,150 Cr net cash).
web_blocks.if_off: If Akkodis Phase 2/3 tranches suffer regulatory delays or Devanahalli DAC/MAC capex absorbs an extra ₹300–₹400 crore of working capital without debt reduction, net cash drops toward ₹750 crore and fair value compresses below ₹1,450/share.

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF: What ₹8,189 Crore Market Cap Already Prices In

web_blocks.html: A Reverse Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) exposes how thin the margin of safety is at ₹1,914.40. Subtracting ₹1,152 crore of pro-forma net cash from Screener's ₹8,189 crore market cap leaves an implied Enterprise Value of ₹7,037 crore. That values the retained core at 41.9x FY27E normalized EBITDA (₹168 crore) and 30.7x FY28E EBITDA (₹229 crore). Those multiples usually belong to debt-free, high-ROCE compounders with 30%+ operating margins.

We model a 12.0% WACC, 5.0% terminal growth, 20% EBIT margin (25% tax), and 35% reinvestment rate for Devanahalli DAC/MAC scale-up. At that hurdle, a ₹7,037 crore EV requires 28% to 30% annual revenue compounding for ten years. Sales must grow from ₹840 crore in FY27E to nearly ₹9,900 crore by FY37 without a working-capital air pocket. Yet over the past eleven years (FY15–FY26), sales compounded at 12.5% [1]. FY26 free cash flow was -₹135 crore, and 3-year ROE averaged 10.8% [1]. Prepaying for 30% decade-long growth before debt drops from ₹698 crore leaves zero room for error.

web_blocks.title: Defence Electronics & ER&D Peer Valuation Matrix

web_blocks.html: Peer comparisons sharpen the relative valuation picture [23][24][25][26]. Pure-play leaders like Data Patterns (40.58% OPM, zero debt, 99.33x P/E) and Astra Microwave (26.67% OPM, +33.68% EPS growth, 75.14x P/E) earn high multiples through radar/EW IP and 16%–22% ROCE [23][24]. State-backed Bharat Electronics (BEL) delivers 26.11% OPM and 36.4% ROCE at 45.79x P/E with zero debt [23]. ER&D peer Cyient trades at 29.8x Screener P/E (₹1,104.90) [23]. AXISCADES trades at 41.9x FY27E EV/EBITDA and 226.15x TradingView P/E [23]. Yet its trailing profile (9.86% OPM, 11.5% ROE, 130 debtor days, ₹698 crore debt) still looks like a leveraged integrator [1].

web_blocks.takeaway: Pure-play defence peers like Astra Microwave (26.7% OPM, 75.1x P/E) and BEL (26.1% OPM, 45.8x P/E) deliver stronger margins and returns on capital without AXISCADES' Ind AS 105 restructuring or ₹698 Cr debt overhang [23][24][26]. Note on Stage reconciliation: the table's Stage column reflects the lagging weekly 30W-SMA screen (STAGE_2), whereas the authoritative daily OHLCV ledger classifies AXISCADES, ASTRAMICRO, and CYIENT as Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) due to 6 distribution days (4 for CYIENT) and daily closes below flattening or falling 50-day SMAs (AXISCADES ₹1,914.40 vs ₹1,938.70 50DMA).

web_blocks.html: Valuation Change Trigger: Our Chapter 7 valuation stance upgrades only if (1) the share price pulls back toward ₹1,450.00 (a re-underwrite alert only, never an automatic buy, requiring Stage 2 base confirmation), and (2) Q3/Q4 FY27 filings confirm gross debt <₹200 crore, net cash >₹900 crore (post-Akkodis settlement), DSO <95 days, and positive TTM FCF.

book_paragraphs: Now you and I step out of the factory and onto the trading floor. On November 13, 2026, two market screens show a puzzling P/E gap for AXISCADES. Screener prints a trailing P/E of 1,993 times, while TradingView shows 226 times. Neither figure is a typo, yet both will mislead you at face value.

Why is the trailing P/E so distorted? AXISCADES is carving out its Heavy Engineering, Automotive, Energy, and Aerospace Services units to Akkodis, effective October 1, 2026. Under Ind AS 105 rules, held-for-sale businesses are stripped out of continuing operations. On a trailing continuing basis, sales sit at ₹831 crore and reported net profit is ₹61 crore. However, ₹69 crore of that profit came from non-operating Other Income, including a ₹61 crore Q2 FY27 swing. H1 FY27 also absorbed ₹21.81 crore of deal fees, ₹11.56 crore of aged receivable provisions, and ₹12 crore of ESOP costs. Stripping Other Income shrinks Screener's profit base to ~₹4 crore, creating the 1,993x ratio.

When trailing earnings break during a carve-out, we use a Sum-of-the-Parts valuation. We split AXISCADES into two clean buckets. First is the retained Defence Electronics, Aerospace Manufacturing, ESAI, and Space business. Second is the net cash left from the ₹2,256 crore Akkodis sale after taxes, fees, and ₹698 crore of September 2026 debt.

Walk through the retained business first. In H1 FY27, continuing sales hit ₹378.95 crore, up 55% year-on-year. With normal second-half defence seasonality, full-year FY27 retained sales should reach ₹840 crore. Once carve-out costs fade, a 20% EBITDA margin gives ₹168 crore of operating profit for FY27. Growing 30% in FY28 to ₹1,092 crore at a 21% margin yields ₹229 crore of EBITDA.

Next, count the Akkodis cash carefully. A headline ₹2,256 crore price never lands free and clear. Deducting roughly 18%—around ₹406 crore—for capital gains taxes, fees, and working-capital true-ups leaves ₹1,850 crore. Subtract the ₹698 crore of gross debt from September 2026. AXISCADES finishes with about ₹1,152 crore in pro-forma net cash, or ₹270 per share across 4.27 crore shares.

Now put both pieces together. We value the retained business generously at 28 times FY28 normalized EBITDA, or ₹6,412 crore (₹1,502 per share). Adding ₹270 per share of net cash brings our SOTP fair value to ₹1,771 per share. That sits 7.5% below the ₹1,914.40 market price. On conservative FY27 numbers at 25x EBITDA, fair value drops near ₹1,207 per share. Only a full-execution bull case at 31x FY28 EBITDA of ₹300 crore lifts fair value toward ₹2,450 per share. That leaves negative asymmetry at today's quote.

A Reverse DCF serves as our sharpest truth serum. Subtract ₹1,152 crore of pro-forma net cash from the ₹8,189 crore market cap. The market is charging ₹7,037 crore today for the retained defence engine alone. That equals 41.9 times FY27 EBITDA and 30.7 times FY28 EBITDA. With a 12% cost of capital, 5% terminal growth, a 20% steady-state EBIT margin, and a 35% reinvestment rate, ₹7,037 crore demands 28% to 30% annual sales growth for ten years. Revenue would have to scale toward ₹9,900 crore by FY37 without a single working-capital setback. Remember that consolidated sales compounded at just 12.5% over the prior eleven years. Even against listed Indian defence peers, the gap is stark. Data Patterns earns a 40.6% operating margin with zero debt at 99.3x earnings. Astra Microwave delivers a 26.7% margin and 33.7% EPS growth at 75.1x earnings. Bharat Electronics earns 36.4% ROCE with zero debt at 45.8x earnings. At ₹1,914.40, AXISCADES asks for a Tier-1 compounder multiple before retiring its ₹698 crore bridge debt or fixing negative free cash flow.

book_subsections.title: Stress-Testing the Reverse DCF: What 30% Decade-Long Growth Actually Demands
paragraphs: Pause on that Reverse DCF implication, because 28% to 30% ten-year growth looks effortless in a spreadsheet. Scaling an ₹840 crore defence platform toward ₹9,900 crore by FY37 requires immense operational execution. Mistral Solutions must convert Ashwini, Virupaksha, and Kusha prototypes into steady multi-year production lots. At the same time, AXISCADES must ramp the Devanahalli Complex, scale aerospace MRO, and build a new satellite bus division.

Every step of that expansion consumes working capital and fixed assets. Indian defence electronics runs through MoD and DPSU acceptance cycles that routinely stretch receivables past 100 days. In FY26, AXISCADES grew consolidated sales just 12% to ₹1,159 crore, yet Debtor Days jumped to 130 and free cash flow hit minus ₹135 crore. Modeling a 35% reinvestment rate and 20% margin for ten straight years leaves zero room for deferrals or cost overruns. If actual compounding settles near 18% to 20%, present value drops well below today's ₹7,037 crore implied EV.

Patience also matters on the Akkodis cash bridge. Multi-phase carve-outs rarely settle in one clean wire transfer. Regulatory approvals, employee true-ups, and taxes routinely trim 15% to 20% off headline deal values across several quarters. Until that cash lands and retires the ₹698 crore debt, crediting ₹1,152 crore of net cash is generous. Even with that generosity, SOTP fair value sits at ₹1,771 per share, below the ₹1,914.40 screen price.

Walk through the sensitivity range to feel how thin the margin of safety is. Valuing the retained core at 25x FY27 normalized EBITDA (₹168 crore) plus ₹952 crore of net cash gives ₹5,152 crore, or ₹1,207 per share. Only in a full-execution bull case—where FY28 EBITDA hits ₹300 crore at 31x—does fair value reach ₹2,450 per share. At ₹1,914.40 today, you are paying for the top half of outcomes before a single rupee of debt is retired.

book_subsections.title: How AXISCADES Stacks Up Against Listed Defence Peers
paragraphs: Peer context reinforces why caution is warranted at ₹1,914.40. On November 13, 2026, Data Patterns trades at 99.3x trailing earnings with a 40.6% operating margin, 21.9% ROCE, and zero debt. Astra Microwave trades at 75.1x earnings with a 26.7% operating margin, 33.7% EPS growth, and 17.2% ROE. Bharat Electronics earns a 36.4% ROCE and 26.1% operating margin at 45.8x earnings with zero debt.

Look across the wider peer table too. Paras Defence trades at 100.1x trailing earnings (₹1,293.30) with a 22.8% operating margin and 41.7% revenue growth. Avantel trades at 222.0x earnings (₹164.76) with a 14.4% operating margin and 5.9% ROE. Centum Electronics—a closer twin in build-to-spec integration—trades at 133.5x TradingView earnings (₹4,481.10) with a 7.8% operating margin and negative 12.5% ROE.

Notice one crucial technical distinction in that peer table. A lagging 30-week average screen still tags AXISCADES, Astra Microwave, and Cyient as Stage 2. Yet the authoritative daily OHLCV ledger classifies all three as Stage 3 (Topping / Pullback) because of distribution days and closes below flattening or falling 50-day moving averages. Meanwhile, ER&D peer Cyient trades at 29.8x Screener earnings (₹1,104.90) with a 9.5% operating margin. AXISCADES asks investors to pay over 41x FY27 normalized EBITDA while free cash flow is negative, debtor days sit at 130, and 3-year ROE averages 10.8%. Great stories deserve respect, not blind prepayment.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Never Pay Peak Multiples Before the Cash Clears
book_callouts.text: When a firm sells half its revenue base to reinvent itself, the stock price often sprints ahead of the bank account. At ₹1,914.40, you are paying for ₹1,152 crore of net Akkodis cash and a decade of 28%–30% compounding before debt is retired or free cash flow turns positive.
